identity.name: Potassium tartrates (cream of tartar)
identity.chemical_class: Tartrate salts of tartaric acid (organic acid salts)

function.mechanism: Provides tartrate anions that modulate acidity/pH and support leavening and formulation functionality in food systems.

adi.basis: Group ADI for L(+)-tartaric acid-tartrates (E334-337, E354), expressed as tartaric acid (EFSA 2020).

efsa.key_finding: EFSA set a group ADI of 240 mg/kg bw/day (as tartaric acid) and reported refined exposure estimates below this ADI.

adi.basis: Group ADI for L(+)-tartaric acid and sodium/potassium/potassium-sodium salts (WHO/JECFA database, latest listed evaluation year 2017).

concerns.summary: Intentional high-dose cream-of-tartar ingestion has caused severe hyperkalemia, including a 2025 report of hyperkalaemic cardiac arrest.
Veterinary literature reports acute kidney injury in dogs after cream-of-tartar/tartaric-acid-rich ingestion; this is a species-specific high-dose signal, not a direct human food-use finding.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA reported no genotoxicity signal for tartaric acid and sodium/potassium salts.
EFSA reported no carcinogenicity indication in chronic rat data at the highest tested dose.
EFSA refined non-brand-loyal exposure estimates did not exceed the group ADI.

adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA population exposure estimates were below ADI; exceedance concern mainly relates to intentional non-food high-dose ingestion.

risk_assessment.rationale: Major regulators permit E336 with ADI/GMP controls, and EFSA exposure estimates are below ADI. Serious adverse outcomes are documented mainly in extreme misuse/overdose scenarios rather than normal dietary exposure.
key_factors: EFSA 2020 group ADI with no exceedance in refined exposure scenarios
No IARC carcinogenic classification entry identified
High-dose case reports show hyperkalemia risk outside normal food use
